## 4. Completely ordinary finite-family TV selection

Freeze all K=J+1 finite models before drawing fresh P holdout and fresh samples
from every model. Define A_ij={x:H_i(x)>H_j(x)}. Each point likelihood is a product
of the finite deterministic model's rational token probabilities, obtained by
its paid convex inference algorithm. Exact rational comparison fixes ties.
No unknown P likelihood, conditional P query, teacher evaluation or TV oracle is
used for those sets. All candidate evaluations and samples are teacher-free.
Each model's convex inference uses fixed deterministic rational tie-breaking,
work caps, interval stopping slack and fallback rules, with no mutable warm-start
state shared between different point queries. Thus H_i(x) names the same law in
the sampler and comparison predicate; it does not depend on evaluation order.

Take n>=log[4(K+1)K^2/delta]/(2e^2) samples from each of P and each H_k.
Hoeffding and a union bound make every empirical probability of each A_ij
accurate to e, except for at most delta/2. Choose k minimizing

    score(k)=max_(i,j)|P_emp(A_ij)-(H_k)_emp(A_ij)|.

For a minimum-TV candidate k*, write v*=TV(P,H_k*). Then score(k*)<=v*+2e.
For the selected k, the true discrepancy |P(A_kk*)-H_k(A_kk*)| is<=v*+4e.
Since A_kk* attains TV(H_k,H_k*),

    TV(P,H_k)<=3v*+4e.                                (4.1)

Set e=epsilon/16. Rational categorical samples have expected polynomial fair-bit
work. If a worst-case cap is desired, use progressive uniform-bit/CDF comparisons
and allocate a union-bound failure across all draws; after sufficiently many
polynomial bits, unresolved comparisons contribute at most the reserved delta.
This changes the failure budget, not which hidden teacher oracle is supplied.

## 5. Always-valid laws and exact finite likelihoods

I specifically challenged whether a bad candidate can be used in a teacher-free
selection tournament. Its finite geometric loops have known work caps and
uniform fallback. Cached token rows are rational probability vectors. For all
|alpha_i|<=C and sum alpha=1, the raw marginal L1 norm is at most SC, so the
clamp normalizer is at most SC+Ob. Every token is therefore at least
b/(SC+Ob), without an approximation event. T's permanent uniform-suffix rule
when the denominator exceeds two is an equally valid simpler completion;
the good-state normalizer is strictly below two, so that rule preserves the
accuracy theorem. Unsupported original-Q queries cannot occur in either case.

The deterministic finite-inference issue is paid constructively, not attributed
to floating CLARABEL. Starting every projection from a uniform feasible vector,
using fixed-precision rational log-gradient rounding, exact rational LP vertices
with fixed ties and a fixed rational FW step gives a known polynomial cap.
The explicit descent/bit argument in LAZY_LAW_AND_COST.md shows that output
coefficient bits depend on cached vertex bounds and the fixed iteration count,
not a repeatedly composed algebraic history from the parent vector. Warranted
log approximations do not wait to decide an exact irrational rounding tie.

Thus, after compilation randomness is frozen, a candidate's point likelihood,
its sampler and the comparison sets use exactly the same deterministic rational
law. An implementation that refreshes solver randomness or changes its law with
cross-query warm starts would not meet this contract. The old floating T8
prototype is not used to establish this new finite-inference theorem.

## 6. Whole unknown-KL composition

SELECTION_RECONSTRUCTION.md independently derives all grid and tournament steps.
The summable confidence schedule gives A_j tau_j<1/100 and x_j<=tau_j^(-2).
Consequently d<=tau_j^(32768) qualifies that fixed-tau candidate. The scientific
log bound uses A0 independently of the grid's confidence-inflated A_j, so no
epsilon-dependent confidence factor is hidden in the noise coefficient.

All candidates are frozen before P holdout and candidate sampling. Pairwise
Yatracos sets use deterministic rational likelihood products, not a target
likelihood or a TV oracle. Estimating each finite set probability by samples and
minimizing the maximum empirical discrepancy yields 3v*+4e. The sample and set-
evaluation costs are explicit polynomials. Applying the three d regimes and
e=epsilon/16 gives the claimed epsilon+256A0^2 d^(1/131072) guarantee, including
the correctly vacuous coarse regime. No KL bound is estimated or needed in the
construction, and no unknown-noise-dependent output precision is requested.

The original exact rational law's expected sampling bit work and the finite
experiment's high-probability bit cap are kept distinct. A finite confidence
union is not claimed to control an unlimited sequence of future outputs.
